title: An item of a list in a script reads by dot and by key, as a source row does
proves: an item of a list of dicts that a <variable> script builds reads as item.field and as item['field'] (#441)
dict(item), str(item) and a membership test give the same result as for a plain dict
a list that a script builds from source rows, and an item of a nested list, read by dot as well
a list that a script module binds stays the script's list of plain dicts, so script code that gets it sees dicts
where= reads an item of a list field of a source row by dot
a field that the item does not have is named in the run error

negatives.name: membership
negatives.expected: copied == True and text == True and found == True
